The most important things to know in your first week: how Quiz Lab is built and shipped, the dev workflow, the pack schema, and how work flows through Studio AI.
Where does the live Quiz Lab app run?
On GitHub Pages as a static site
On an AWS server behind an API
Quiz Lab is served from GitHub Pages under the base path /product-demo — a fully prerendered static site, not Vercel (Architecture Overview).
Which framework and adapter is Quiz Lab built with?
Quiz Lab is a SvelteKit 2 app built with Vite and @sveltejs/adapter-static, so it prerenders to a fully client-side static site (Architecture Overview).
Which database stores Quiz Lab's content and leaderboards?
There is no database — all content ships in the build

There is no server runtime and no database; all quiz content ships inside the static build. Docs that mention Postgres or Vercel are out-of-date marketing, not the live architecture (Architecture Overview).
What single action ships a change to production?
Merging a pull request to main
Pushing to a release branch each Friday

Merging a PR to main is what ships: a GitHub Actions workflow then builds the site and publishes it to Pages. There is no separate deploy step or manual release (Engineering Handbook; Architecture Overview).
Where in the repo do quiz pack JSON files live?
Packs are one JSON file each in app/src/lib/data/packs/. The old static/quizzes/ location belongs to the deprecated v0 format and must not be used (Pack Authoring Guide; Architecture Overview).
How does a new pack get added to the app?
Drop a JSON file in the packs directory and open a PR

You add a pack by dropping a JSON file in app/src/lib/data/packs/ and opening a PR — no backend changes or migrations, because there is no backend. It appears on the next merge to main (Architecture Overview; Product Vision & Glossary).
How many answer choices must each question have?
Every question's choices array must have exactly 4 options (Pack Authoring Guide). The old v0 format allowed any length, but it is superseded.
How is the correct answer recorded on a question?
A `correct` string holding the answer text
A `correctIndex` integer from 0 to 3 into choices
A boolean flag on the right choice
It is always the first item in choices
The current schema uses correctIndex, an integer 0–3 that indexes into choices. Storing the answer as a `correct` string is the deprecated v0 shape and is invalid (Pack Authoring Guide).
What are the valid values for a question's `difficulty` field?
difficulty is an integer of 1, 2, or 3, rendered as ★ to ★★★. Packs should also mix difficulties rather than make every question level 1 (Pack Authoring Guide).
How many questions should a pack contain?
The style rules call for 10–15 questions per pack, with mixed difficulty (Pack Authoring Guide).
Factual and grounded in a source document
Explanations are required, non-empty, and must be factual and grounded in a source — for harder questions you cite the source. Inventing facts is not allowed (Pack Authoring Guide).
In Studio AI, what is an 'idea'?
A hypothesis to validate, broken into PR-sized tasks
An idea is a hypothesis with a technical design; it is broken into discrete, PR-sized tasks linked to it as ideaSubtasks (Engineering Handbook; Studio AI SDLC & MCP).
What is the branching and merge policy for the repo?
Commit directly to main, revert if broken
Gitflow with a long-lived develop branch
Trunk-based: land work via a reviewed, squash-merged PR; never commit directly to main
Merge a release branch once a quarter
We practice trunk-based development: main is always releasable, and every change lands through a short-lived branch and a reviewed, squash-merged PR (Engineering Handbook).
When an agent picks up a task with work_on_next_task, what does it receive in addition to the task spec?
Nothing — it must search for everything
A list of every document in the knowledge base

At pickup, Studio AI injects the task's curated context — the small 'neighborhood' of relevant documents attached to the task or inherited from its parent idea — so the agent doesn't have to go discover it (Studio AI SDLC & MCP; Engineering Handbook).
Roughly how many documents make up a well-curated context 'neighborhood' for a task?
About 5 — the minimum needed and nothing else
A good neighborhood is about 5 documents — the smallest set the agent needs and nothing else. Curating it up front is the biggest lever on output quality (Studio AI SDLC & MCP; Engineering Handbook).
From the 1992 inaugural season to today — how well do you know the EPL?
Who is the Premier League's all-time top scorer?
Alan Shearer scored 260 Premier League goals, mostly with Newcastle United.
Which club won the inaugural Premier League title in the 1992–93 season?
Manchester United, managed by Sir Alex Ferguson, won the first ever Premier League.
Erling Haaland joined Manchester City in 2022 from which club?
Haaland transferred from Borussia Dortmund and won the Golden Boot in his first PL season.
Which stadium is home to Liverpool FC?
Anfield has been Liverpool's home since 1892.
Who has won the most Premier League Golden Boots?
Both Henry and Shearer are tied
Thierry Henry and Alan Shearer are tied on four Golden Boots each.
Salah captains the Egyptian national team.
Brighton & Hove Albion, named for their coastal home.
Which player holds the record for most Premier League appearances?
Gareth Barry made 653 PL appearances across Aston Villa, Manchester City, Everton, and West Brom.
Which manager led Leicester City to their fairytale 2015–16 title?
Claudio Ranieri's Leicester won the title at 5000-1 preseason odds.
What is the largest stadium currently used in the Premier League by capacity?
Which club won four Premier League titles in a row from 2020–21 to 2023–24?
Manchester City's four consecutive titles is a PL record.
Newcastle United play their home games at:
St James' Park has been Newcastle's home since 1892.
Who is Arsenal's all-time leading goal scorer in the Premier League era?
Thierry Henry is Arsenal's all-time top scorer with 228 goals across all competitions.
In what year was the Premier League founded?
The Premier League was founded in February 1992.
Which goalkeeper has the most Premier League clean sheets all-time?

Fog, hills, and Painted Ladies — how well do you know the City by the Bay?
Which San Francisco neighborhood was the epicenter of the 1967 'Summer of Love' counterculture movement?
Haight-Ashbury — the intersection of Haight and Ashbury streets — drew tens of thousands of young people during the 1967 Summer of Love (Wikipedia: 'Summer of Love').
Which neighborhood is historically known as San Francisco's 'Little Italy'?
North Beach has been the city's Italian-American enclave since the late 1800s, and still hosts the annual North Beach Festival (Wikipedia: 'North Beach, San Francisco').
Which San Francisco Bay island housed a federal penitentiary from 1934 to 1963?
Alcatraz operated as a federal maximum-security prison from 1934 to 1963 and is now managed by the National Park Service (nps.gov/alca; Wikipedia: 'Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary').
Coit Tower atop Telegraph Hill was funded by a 1929 bequest from which San Francisco socialite?
Lillie Hitchcock Coit left a third of her estate to the city 'for the purpose of adding to the beauty of San Francisco'; the tower opened in 1933 (Wikipedia: 'Coit Tower').
Which San Francisco bakery, founded in 1849, claims to be the city's original sourdough?
Boudin Bakery has baked sourdough in San Francisco since 1849 using a mother dough that traces back to its founding (boudinbakery.com/our-story; Wikipedia: 'Boudin Bakery').
Which seafood stew, created by Italian immigrant fishermen at Fisherman's Wharf in the late 1800s, is considered a San Francisco original?
Cioppino was developed by Ligurian fishermen working out of Fisherman's Wharf, combining the day's catch with tomato and wine (Wikipedia: 'Cioppino').
How many hairpin turns does Lombard Street's famously 'crookedest' block between Hyde and Leavenworth contain?
The one-block stretch of Lombard between Hyde and Leavenworth has eight tight switchback turns paved in red brick in 1922 to tame the block's 27% grade (Wikipedia: 'Lombard Street, San Francisco').
San Francisco's cable cars are pulled by an underground cable that moves at what constant speed?

All four cables run continuously beneath the streets at a constant 9.5 mph; cars start and stop when the gripman engages or releases a grip on the cable (SFMTA: 'Cable Car System'; Wikipedia: 'San Francisco cable car system').
Harvey Milk made history in 1977 when he was elected to which San Francisco governing body, becoming the first openly gay person elected to public office in California?

Milk won a seat on the San Francisco Board of Supervisors in November 1977 — San Francisco has no city council; the Board of Supervisors is its 11-member legislative body. He was assassinated alongside Mayor George Moscone the following year (Wikipedia: 'Harvey Milk').

After the 1906 earthquake destroyed San Francisco's Chinatown, community leaders fended off pressure to relocate residents to Hunters Point and instead rebuilt in place. What distinctive feature did the rebuilt architecture deliberately emphasize?
"Oriental"-style pagoda roofs and ornamentation aimed at attracting tourists
Beaux-Arts facades that matched the surrounding city
Industrial warehouses for the import-export trade

Businessman Look Tin Eli organized the rebuild and hired architects T. Paterson Ross and A.W. Burgren to design Chinatown with deliberately exoticized pagoda roofs, dragon motifs, and colored tiles — the strategy was to make the neighborhood a tourist draw, which helped keep it from being displaced. The look that still defines Grant Avenue today is the result (Wikipedia: 'Chinatown, San Francisco', '1906 earthquake' section).
